videos.title: Give Me 18 Minutes and You'll Finally Let Go
videos.description:
Most of us already know when something isn't working. The hard part is not starting over. It's letting go.

In this episode, Jay Shetty talks about why we hold on to relationships, jobs and dreams we have already outgrown. He explains the bias that makes a loss feel about twice as strong as an equal gain, and the trap that keeps us paying for years we have already spent.

He shares the one question that removes nostalgia from a hard decision, and why what we really hold on to is often the person we got to be inside a situation, not the situation itself.

And he talks about the hidden cost of staying, what research on regret says we regret most over time, and why a feeling is not an instruction.

Learn why your brain protects a life you no longer want. And learn the question to ask before you stay in anything.

videos.title: HILARY DUFF: What Lizzie McGuire’s Smile Was Hiding
videos.description:
Hilary Duff on the family truth she spent years tiptoeing around.

In this episode, Hilary Duff and Jay Shetty talk about the songs on her first album in over a decade, and the real life behind them. She explains why, as painful as it is to share, she could only write about what she has lived through.

She looks back at growing up in the public eye from the age of 10: the comments on her body as a teenager, the innocence she says she lost by 15, and the mom who kept her grounded. She opens up about divorce, co-parenting, and why a kind partner was so hard to accept.

And she talks about being the peacemaker when her parents split up, the father she wishes would show up, and why some of the hardest relationships are in your own family.

Learn why she calls it a raw nerve. And learn what she still hopes for the person she grew up with.

videos.title: Essentials: Nicotine's Effects on the Brain & Body & How to Quit Smoking or Vaping
videos.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, I explain how nicotine affects the brain and body, including how it increases dopamine, acetylcholine and norepinephrine to boost motivation, focus and alertness, suppresses appetite and raises heart rate and blood pressure. I distinguish nicotine itself from its delivery methods — smoking, vaping, dipping and snuffing — and explain their serious health risks, why vaping is especially habit-forming and why quitting is so difficult. I also discuss science-based tools to quit smoking or vaping, including clinical hypnosis, prescription medication and nicotine replacement strategies, and how to get through the critical first week of withdrawal.

videos.title: Every Contractor Used This Trick on Me
videos.description:
People are more likely to act a certain way when you label them as the kind of person who would. It's a subtle form of psychological influence that taps into our desire to stay consistent with how others see us.

From compliments disguised as favors to carefully crafted sales pitches, these tactics show up in everyday interactions more often than you might think.
